I am pretty sure that any type of autonomous driving won't be ready in the next decade or more. Outside a closed course with a finite number of scenarios, there are just too many variables. Both Google and Musk are overestimating the reliability of their systems, and Google's recent crash with a bus only partially demonstrates this fact. Sure, it's impressive technology, but it would require infrastructure changes to ensure safe conditions. For example, special autonomous "speedways" could be built that will only allow autonomous cars that have been serviced recently to enter. The speedways would have to be well-maintained, which could be aided by automatic reporting from vehicles on the route but also by manual inspection of the road. They would be treated as railways with convoys of cars. The lead car and all cars behind it should be able to stop quickly without creating a pileup.

Driver assistance like lane departure warnings and the like may develop rapidly. Eventually, it may be shown that drivers make too many mistakes versus the AI, which has an infinitesimally small chance of making one. That sounds great, but I would definitely want to be behind the wheel on back roads and other open courses.
